New in 0.1.9

Updating from 0.1.8 or earlier? This one needs a manual download. TimeCal's internal app identifier changed in this release, which macOS treats as a different app, so the automatic updater cannot replace your copy and will fail if it tries. Download 0.1.9 from trytimecal.com/downloads, drag it into Applications, and replace the old copy. Your license is safe and you will not need to re-enter your key. This is a one time step: updates after this one install themselves as usual.

TimeCal is in beta and now for sale. This release adds two things worth having and fixes a handful of things that were quietly wrong.

  • Your working day, shaded. Turn on "Shade hours outside the working day" in Settings, General, and the evenings and early mornings recede so your actual day is the bright band. Set the range to whatever yours is, including one that runs past midnight. Off by default, and it steps out of the way when you zoom out far enough that the bands would just be a wash.
  • Hover the now-line for the time. Point at the red line anywhere along its height and the current time appears at its marker. Most useful when you are zoomed out far enough that the header no longer tells you.
  • Make calendars on your Mac. "On My Mac" is now offered when you add a calendar, even if you do not have a local calendar yet, and it is the default. Local calendars sync nowhere and cannot disturb anything shared with you, which makes them the safe place to keep the calendars you are only keeping for yourself. Your other accounts are still in the list.
  • The all-day band tidies itself. Deleting one of several stacked multi-day events left a gap where it had been until you scrolled or clicked something. The band now closes up on its own.
  • Header labels give way. The pinned label at the left edge now slides aside as the next one arrives, instead of being covered part-way through.
  • Notes placeholder lines up. The cursor in an empty notes field now sits exactly where "Add Notes" says typing will start.
  • The right pointer in the guide. The Guide showed a different Pointer icon than the toolbar does.
  • Licensing. License keys are now checked against TimeCal specifically rather than the store account they came from. Existing keys, including beta keys, are unaffected.
  • Two prompts on first launch after upgrading. Because of the identifier change above, macOS asks permission to use your saved license and wants your keychain password for it. Choose Always Allow and it will not ask again. It will also ask for calendar access once more. Both are one time. If you do deny the keychain prompt, TimeCal now says so plainly instead of behaving as though you had never bought it.

New in 0.1.8

A polish release. Lots of small things that were slightly off are now right, and rule badges learned a genuinely useful trick.

  • Opens on your week. A fresh launch now lands on week zoom with today at the left edge, instead of a zoomed-in day. While the app stays open your view stays where you left it.
  • Badges can open links. A rule badge can now be a button. In the rule editor, turn on "Badge opens the event's first link" and clicking the badge on an event jumps straight to its link, the Zoom call, the booking page, whatever the event carries. Add a match pattern to pick a specific link, like zoom.us, when an event has several. If no link is found the click just opens the event as usual.
  • Who is coming. Invitees now show their reply the way you would expect: a green check for accepted, red for declined, a quiet question mark for no reply yet, with the organizer and optional guests labeled.
  • Long notes scroll. Notes that used to clip past a few lines now scroll inside the popover, including on read-only calendars. Provider-generated novels are finally readable in place.
  • Snappier event popover. Typing in the event editor no longer drags while the timeline animates behind it.
  • Header labels pin properly. The day and hour labels now stick to the left edge with a clean backing, the way the month label always has. No more clipped digits hanging off the edge.
  • A nicer front door. The unlock screen has been redesigned, with a wider key field so your whole license key is visible when you paste it.
  • Emoji badges, unboxed. An emoji badge now stands on its own instead of being squeezed into a colored disc.
  • Quieter tooltips. Toolbar tooltips are now just the name and the hotkey. The Guide keeps the full explanations, and now lists the N key for follow mode.

Feedback

Send anything, bugs, ideas, confusion, to evan@trytimecal.com.
